title: If You Plant a Seed
author: Kadir Nelson

hero.name: Rabbit (If You Plant a Seed)
hero.description: Round, soft-furred brown rabbit character from the cover, illustrated in Kadir Nelson's realistic painterly style
hero.source_note: Generic rabbit — Boardmaker rabbit symbol is acceptable; if a closer match to Nelson's style is desired, source from TPT or Creative Fabrica

ambiguous.issue: Could mean the action of planting (verb) or a living plant (noun)
ambiguous.reason: The book is centrally about the act of planting a seed, so the verb sense is primary; use a Boardmaker symbol showing a hand putting something in soil

notes: This book's core message is about kindness and sharing versus selfishness — 'share', 'kind', 'selfish', and 'fight' are thematically essential and give students language to discuss the social-emotional content. 'Tomato' is the main fruit that grows and is contested in the story (more specific and picturable than generic 'fruit'). 'Grow' captures the central cause-and-effect concept. The rabbit and bird are the two main characters; rabbit is chosen as hero (cover character). The bird is a secondary character included in fringe_11. 'Happy' anchors the positive resolution. Existing activity_images vocab (seed, plant, soil, pot, sun, sprout, fruit, bird, rabbit, rain, garden) overlaps well — 'seed', 'plant', 'garden', and 'bird' can reuse existing icons. 'Tomato' is preferred over 'fruit' for specificity to this book.

matching.note: Min 4 approved stems, no hard cap
